d.g: In the Big Bang theory, the hot and dense plasma that made up the matter in the cosmos following the initial baryogenesis at an early stage of its expansion and cooling, from which the first atoms formed and photons decoupled. The emission of photons in this phase is regarded as the source of the cosmic microwave background.
d.x: The ylem was the primordial flux of neutrons out of which all else emerged.

ylem.e: Resuscitation of Middle English ylem, from Medieval Latin hȳlem, accusative of hȳlē (“matter, the fundamental matter of all things; the matter of the body”) (whence English hyle), a transliteration of Ancient Greek ὕλη (húlē, “wood; material, substance; matter”). …

d.g: The fragrant flower of a tropical tree (Cananga odorata) native to southeast Asia.
An essential oil derived from this flower used in aromatherapy and perfumes.
d.x: Essential oils such as jasmine, rose, vetiver, ilang-ilang, iris, vanilla, sandalwood or lavender cannot be synthesised in the laboratory.

d.g: The tree (Cananga odorata) on which ylang ylang flowers grow.

ylang ylang.e: Via Early Modern Spanish, from Tagalog ilang-ilang, from either ilang (“wilderness”) or ilang-ilan (“rare”).

d.x: Games for the harmonics, (children), YL's and XYL's and the OM's, plus free soda for all.

YL.e: In radio sense: short for young lady.
